title: The uncle, Monday
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Monday. Wood draws the uncle. The chair, the line, the bay behind. The uncle lets him. He says 'more at the bottom' and it's a joke now. Wood draws the joke.

panels.composition: The chair by the shack. The UNCLE in it, the oxygen line, looking at the bay. WOOD on a pot with the pad, close. BARNABY at the chair's leg.

image.prompt: an old man in a lawn chair with an oxygen line looking at a bay while a young man draws him from close by on a crab pot, a small dog at the chair's leg, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The pad: the uncle, in the chair, exact. Not a pear. A man.

image.prompt: close on a drawing pad with a careful ink portrait of an old man in a lawn chair, not caricatured, black and white, no words
an old weathered man glancing sideways at a drawing, dry, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood adding more at the bottom. The uncle, wider by a stroke. The joke, drawn. The uncle nodding. Monday.

image.prompt: a young man adding a stroke to a drawing of an old man in a lawn chair who nods, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Monday. 'Draw it, then.' The joke, drawn.
